items.label: text
items.text: Safety Note: Wear eye protection and take care not to get burned when raising the crucible lid with tongs. The crucible will stay very hot for some time.

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEYPOINT

items.label: text
items.text: How do we know when the reaction has finished? We can generally see when there is no more reaction because nothing is happening in the crucible. We can also check by weighing the crucible and contents, then heating it and weighing again. If the mass is higher when we weigh it again then this indicates that a reaction has occurred. We keep heating and weighing until the mass stays constant.

items.label: section_header
items.text: ACTIVITY 3

items.label: section_header
items.text: PRACTICAL: INVESTIGATING THE FORMULA OF A METAL OXIDE BY COMBUSTION

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 5.12 Apparatus for determining the formula of magnesium oxide

items.label: text
items.text: We can find the formula of magnesium oxide by burning magnesium in oxygen and looking at how the mass changes. The following procedure is usually used:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Weigh a crucible with a lid.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Place a piece of magnesium ribbon about 10 cm long in the crucible and weigh the crucible and contents.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Set up the apparatus as shown in Figure 5.12.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Heat the crucible strongly (a roaring flame).

items.label: list_item
items.text: Lift the lid every few seconds.

items.label: list_item
items.text: When the reaction is finished, allow the crucible and contents to cool.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Weigh the crucible and contents.

items.label: text
items.text: When the magnesium burns it does so with a bright white flame. Magnesium oxide, a white powder, is produced in the reaction.

items.label: text
items.text: A lid is placed on the crucible to prevent the white powder (magnesium oxide) escaping but the lid must be lifted every few seconds to allow oxygen into the crucible to react with the magnesium.

items.label: text
items.text: A set of results for this practical could be:

items.label: table
items.text:
| mass of empty crucible/g                           |   32.46 |
|----------------------------------------------------|---------|
| mass of crucible + magnesium/g                     |   32.70 |
| mass of crucible + contents at end of experiment/g |   32.86 |

items.label: text
items.text: We can work out the mass of magnesium by subtracting the mass of the crucible from the mass of the crucible + magnesium:

items.label: formula
items.text: \ m a s s \, o f \, m a g n e s i u m = 3 2 . 7 0 - 3 2 . 4 6 = 0 . 2 4 \, g

items.label: text
items.text: The reason that the mass increases is because the magnesium combines with the oxygen in the air. The mass of magnesium oxide is greater than the mass of just magnesium due to the extra oxygen.
